## Template overview {.rl-bg-light}

### What this template includes

- Manual cover and closing slides
- Normal slides with color variants
- Big centered title slides
- Split 30/70 slides
- Animated SVG background slides
- Inline color, highlight and underline utilities

Use this file as a [visual catalogue]{.rl-mark-yellow} of the available slide styles.

## Slide grammar {.rl-bg-pearl}

### Use only `##` for real slides

- `## Title` → normal slide
- `## Title {.rl-bg-light}` → light slide
- `## Title {.rl-big-title .rl-bg-navy .rl-word-aqua}` → big centered title
- `## Title {.rl-split-30-70 .rl-dark}` → split slide
- `## Title {.theme-title1}` → animated SVG title slide
- `## Cover {.rl-cover ...}` → cover or closing slide

## COVER VARIANTS {.rl-big-title .rl-bg-navy .rl-word-aqua}

## Template overview {.rl-bg-light}

### What this template includes

- Manual cover and closing slides
- Normal slides with color variants
- Big centered title slides
- Split 30/70 slides
- Animated SVG background slides
- Inline color, highlight and underline utilities

Use this file as a [visual catalogue]{.rl-mark-yellow} of the available slide styles.


## Slide grammar {.rl-bg-pearl}

### Use only `##` for real slides

- `## Title` → normal slide
- `## Title {.rl-bg-light}` → normal light slide
- `## Title {.rl-bg-teal}` → soft aqua slide
- `## Title {.rl-bg-navy}` → dark high-contrast slide
- `## Title {.rl-big-title .rl-bg-navy .rl-word-aqua}` → big centered title
- `## Title {.rl-split-30-70 .rl-dark}` → split slide
- `## Title {.theme-title1}` → animated SVG title slide
- `## Cover {.rl-cover ...}` → cover or closing slide

Do not use `#` headings in this template. Use `###` and `####` only inside slides.


## BIG TITLE SLIDES {.rl-big-title .rl-bg-navy .rl-word-aqua}

### For transitions, sections and memorable moments


## METHODS {.rl-big-title .rl-bg-dark .rl-word-gold .rl-big-xl}

### Large title using the gold accent


## RESULTS {.rl-big-title .rl-bg-light .rl-word-petrol .rl-big-xl}

### Light background with strong dark word


## TAKEAWAYS {.rl-big-title .rl-bg-gold .rl-word-ink}

### Warm accent slide for final messages


## Default dark slide

### Default slide style

This is the default normal slide. It uses the [petrol brand color]{.rl-text-aqua .rl-bold} as background and light text.

- Use this for standard explanations.
- Keep the content short.
- Use highlights only when needed.

The [main contribution]{.rl-mark-yellow} can be highlighted, while [technical terms]{.rl-text-gold .rl-bold} can use color.


## Light slide example {.rl-bg-light}

### Clean academic background

#### Smaller subtitle

This variant is useful for dense technical content, figures, tables or diagrams.

The [main idea]{.rl-mark-cyan} is easy to emphasize. You can also use [rose text]{.rl-text-rose .rl-bold}, [orange text]{.rl-text-orange}, or [underlined concepts]{.rl-u-petrol .rl-bold}.


## Aqua slide {.rl-bg-teal}

### Soft scientific background

This is useful for biomedical, rehabilitation or soft robotics sections.

The controller achieved [safe tracking]{.rl-u-aqua .rl-bold} without [thermal saturation]{.rl-mark-pink}.

You can combine:

- [highlight yellow]{.rl-mark-yellow}
- [highlight pink]{.rl-mark-pink}
- [highlight green]{.rl-mark-green}
- [highlight purple]{.rl-mark-purple}


## Pearl gray slide {.rl-bg-pearl}

### Neutral, calm and readable

Use this background when a pure white slide feels too bright but a colored slide feels too strong.

A [soft marker]{.rl-mark-cyan} and a [gold underline]{.rl-u-gold .rl-bold} work well here.


## Navy slide {.rl-bg-navy}

### High contrast slide

Use this for important messages or short technical summaries.

- [Aqua]{.rl-text-aqua .rl-bold} works well on navy.
- [Gold]{.rl-text-gold .rl-bold} works well for key numbers.
- [Rose]{.rl-text-rose} adds contrast.

> Blockquotes also adapt to the slide color system.


## Gold slide {.rl-bg-gold}

### Warm accent for conclusions

Use this slide sparingly, for one key idea, conclusion or memorable statement.

The [final takeaway]{.rl-mark-yellow .rl-bold} should be short and clear.


## Inline utilities {.rl-bg-light}

### Text colors, highlights and underlines

This template includes several inline classes:

- [Petrol text]{.rl-text-petrol}
- [Aqua text]{.rl-text-aqua}
- [Blue text]{.rl-text-blue}
- [Gold text]{.rl-text-gold}
- [Orange text]{.rl-text-orange}
- [Rose text]{.rl-text-rose}
- [Coral text]{.rl-text-coral}
- [Green text]{.rl-text-green}
- [Violet text]{.rl-text-violet}

You can write [bold colored text]{.rl-text-rose .rl-bold}, [highlighted results]{.rl-mark-yellow}, or [underlined key ideas]{.rl-u-aqua .rl-bold}.


## Code and equations {.rl-bg-light}

### Example with code

```{r, echo=TRUE}
model <- lm(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars)
summary(model)
```

Inline code such as `u_pid[k]` uses the slide code color.

You can also write mathematical content:

$$
e[k] = r[k] - y[k]
$$


## 30/70 split, dark right {.rl-split-30-70 .rl-dark}

- Left panel: slide title
- Right panel: main content
- Useful for concept explanation
- Works well with bullets, quotes and code

This layout is good when the title should behave like a visual anchor.

> The right side can contain the real technical explanation.


## 30/70 split, light right {.rl-split-30-70 .rl-light}

- Dark petrol left panel
- Pale aqua right panel
- Good for readable technical explanations
- Suitable for short paragraphs and lists

The [important concept]{.rl-mark-yellow} can be highlighted inside the content area.


## 30/70 split, teal style {.rl-split-30-70 .rl-teal}

- Stronger RoboticsLab identity
- Good for system overview
- Good for architecture slides
- Good for paper contribution slides

Use this slide when you want something more distinctive than a normal slide.


## 30/70 split, navy style {.rl-split-30-70 .rl-navy}

- Light left panel
- Dark right panel
- Good for dramatic contrasts
- Useful for a key result or final concept

The [gold accent]{.rl-text-gold .rl-bold} works well on the dark side.


## Animated title background 1 {.theme-title1 .rl-up}

### Use for section openings


## Animated title background 2 {.theme-title2 .rl-theme-light}

### Another centered title background


## Animated section background 1 {.theme-section1}

### Text and code example

This slide uses an animated SVG background and reserves content space on the left.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
plot(cars)
```


## Animated section background 2 {.theme-section2}

### Subtitle

This style is useful for section transitions or short explanations.

Quarto enables you to combine text, figures, code and custom visual layouts.


## Animated section background 3 {.theme-section3}

### Another subtitle

This variant places the content further to the right.

Use it when the visual background has stronger elements on the left.


## Generic animated slide 1 {.theme-slide1}

### Normal slide with custom SVG background

This slide uses a full-slide animated SVG background.


## Generic animated slide 2 {.theme-slide2}

### Left-offset content

This variant shifts content to avoid visual elements in the background.

- Item one
- Item two
- Item three


## Generic animated slide 3 {.theme-slide3}

### Another left-offset content slide

Use these variants when a specific background image requires a custom content position.


## Generic animated slide 4 {.theme-slide4}

### Top-offset title

This variant moves the title down slightly.


## Generic animated slide 5 {.theme-slide5}

### Small left offset

This variant uses a smaller left offset.


## Generic animated slide 6 {.theme-slide6}

### Small left offset

Suitable for backgrounds with mild visual elements.


## Generic animated slide 7 {.theme-slide7}

### Top-offset title

Use for visual transition slides.


## Generic animated slide 8 {.theme-slide8}

### Top-offset title

Another visual slide variant.


## Custom QMD background {.rl-bg-light background-image="_extensions/roboticslab-slides/backgrounds/cover-srar.svg" background-size="cover" background-position="center"}

### Per-slide background image

This shows how to attach a one-off background image from the QMD heading.

Use this only when a specific presentation needs a unique visual background.


## Recommended slide sequence {.rl-bg-light}

### Suggested structure for a 5–6 minute conference talk

1. Cover
2. Motivation
3. Problem
4. Proposed idea
5. System architecture
6. Control strategy
7. Experimental setup
8. Main results
9. Takeaways
10. Closing

Use only a few highly visual slides. Keep most technical slides clean.
